content.text: As we edge closer to the 2026 FIFA World Cup, bookmakers are assessing their odds on who will take home the coveted trophy. With the tournament set to take place across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, excitement is palpable among fans and bettors alike. France finds itself as a favourite, with their current odds reflecting an implied probability of around 20-22%. In contrast, Spain has climbed the ranks after their Euro 2024 success, while Argentina's odds have begun to drift as concerns mount over Lionel Messi's age and fitness. In this analysis, we'll dive deep into the current betting landscape, the reasoning behind these odds, and the implications for savvy bettors.
Current Outright Odds Across Major Bookmakers

Assessing the outright odds from key sportsbooks reveals a fascinating picture of the competition. At Bet365, France is typically priced between 4.5 and 5.0, yielding an implied probability of approximately 20-22%. Following them closely is Spain, whose odds range from 5.5 to 6.5, translating to an implied 15-18%. The recent victory in Euro 2024 has significantly bolstered their standing, demonstrating the powerful influence of momentum in tournament play.

On the other hand, Argentina's odds have moved to around 7.0-8.0, indicating an implied probability of 12-14%. The pressure of defending their title is compounded by the aging of pivotal players like Messi, making their path to success appear increasingly complicated. Brazil follows closely with odds set at 8.0-9.0 (11-12% implied), while England consistently sits at around 8.5-10.0. Bookmakers have historically discounted England's chances relative to their talent, largely due to the psychological burden that comes with competing in high-stakes tournaments.
Historically, every defending champion since 2002 has been eliminated in the Round of 16 in their subsequent World Cup.
The Square Competition: Germany, Portugal, and Beyond

Germany’s odds currently range from 12 to 15, implying a 6-8% chance of winning. Despite their recent struggles, the German machine is known for its resilience, making it unwise to count them out entirely. Portugal, with odds between 18 and 25, is priced around 4-5%, largely due to their mix of experience and youthful talent, including players like João Félix and Bruno Fernandes.

The Netherlands, sitting at an odds range of 25-35, and Belgium, a longer shot at 50 or better, present intriguing cases. The 'Golden Generation' of Belgium seems to be fading, yet they have enough individual brilliance to upset stronger teams. The unpredictability of tournaments makes it essential to consider not just the top-tier teams but also the potential dark horses.
Betting markets are usually 90-95% efficient at the major-favourite level.
Dark Horse Value Bets: Japan and Colombia

As the 2026 World Cup approaches, conversations around dark horse candidates have intensified. Japan, whose ability to upset larger footballing nations is evidenced by their shocking victories over Germany and Spain during the 2022 World Cup, is drawing attention from sharp bettors. Their current odds hover around a staggering 150-1, with an implied probability of under 1%. This figure may seem steep, but for a team that has proven its competitive edge, the value is evident.

Similarly, Colombia's odds are placed between 80-100, buoyed by the impressive form of players like Luís Díaz. Uruguay, with odds ranging from 60-80 founded on the unique talents of Federico Valverde, also represents a compelling value pick. These teams illustrate how the betting markets can overlook legitimate threats as they focus predominantly on the recognised giants.
Value tends to exist in the 50-150 range for legitimate dark horses.
The Mbappé and Bellingham Factor

With Kylian Mbappé's current Golden Boot odds priced between 5-7, football fans are eagerly awaiting how his performance will influence France’s World Cup run. Similarly, England's Jude Bellingham has seen odds between 8-12 for the Golden Ball, thanks to his rise as a midfield maestro. The expectations are high for these young talents, and their ability to perform under pressure could decisively impact the tournament.

Harry Kane, at odds of 7-9, stands ready to commandeer England's forward line, while Norway's Erling Haaland comes in at 12-15, not least due to doubts surrounding his team’s ability to navigate to deep rounds of the tournament. Such intricacies illustrate the interconnectedness of player performance and overall national success.
Why Bookmakers Favor France – and Other Considerations

Bookmakers' confidence in France stems from a confluence of factors: a deep squad teeming with talent, a peak-aged Kylian Mbappé, and a proven managerial regime under Didier Deschamps. France's historical success, crowned when they won the 2018 World Cup and finished as finalists in 2022, provides them with a consistency premium that cannot be overlooked.

Despite España’s Euro 2024 victory leading many to believe in their potential, the grueling nature of the World Cup must also be considered. Unlike the six matches of the European Championship, teams must navigate seven matches in a World Cup, testing their tactical and physical endurance. Possession-based football, while effective in short bursts, may face a different level of scrutiny over an extended tournament. These nuances shape the odds, further differentiating the established favorites from their challengers.
The Impact of Tournament Structure and Final Thoughts

The 2026 World Cup's expanded format, accommodating 48 teams, introduces additional unpredictability. The knockout rounds will commence at the Round of 32 rather than the usual Round of 16, inherently increasing the variance throughout the tournament. Such changes could disproportionately affect the favorites, who must maintain consistency throughout more matches.

In conclusion, France's odds of approximately 20% implied probability seem just about right, while Spain's range of 15-18% reflects their rising stock. The other contenders offer a mix of risk and value, largely depending on the individual betting strategy and understanding of market biases. As the World Cup approaches, remember that significant movements in odds often correlate with key team news—any injuries to leading stars like Mbappé, Rodri, or Pedri could drastically shake up the odds. Always remember to wager responsibly; the World Cup is not only the most-watched sporting event but also one of the most bet upon, and most bettors ultimately find themselves on the losing side.
